Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 results: Net profit rises 1.25% to ₹312 crore
items.summary:
Non-bank lender Sammaan Capital on Saturday reported a 1.25 per cent increase in its September quarter net profit to Rs 312.34 crore compared to Rs 308.47 crore in the same quarter of last year.
The company had reported a net profit of Rs 243.30 crore in the preceding June quarter.
Its total income declined to Rs 1,850.85 crore in the reporting quarter from Rs 2,260.52 crore in the year-ago period, which included a decline in the core interest income to Rs 1,161.26 crore from Rs 1,449.02 crore.
Total expenses also declined to Rs 1,426.28 crore from Rs 1,835.49 crore in the year-ago period, as per a regulatory filing.
Assets under management grew by 5 per cent to Rs 59,188 crore as of end-June 2026, driven by a 62 per cent jump in disbursements to Rs 6,278 crore. It aims to increase AUM to Rs 70,000 crore by March 2027.
The company added more branches during the quarter to take its overall network to 245 as of September 30, and is aiming to take the same to 270 by end of the fiscal

MSCI adds LIC, Coforge, Adani Green and Meesho to Emerging Markets Index
MSCI adds LIC, Coforge, Adani Green, Meesho to index
items.summary: Mumbai: Index provider MSCI has added four local stocks - Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Coforge, Adani Green Energy and Meesho - to its Emerging Markets Standard Index in the November 2026 review. PI Industries has been excluded.The changes will take effect on November 30. According to Nuvama, Coforge's inclusion could attract passive inflows of around $630 million. LIC, Adani Green Energy and Meesho could see inflows of $468 million, $348 million and $307 million, respectively. PI Industries' exclusion could lead to outflows of about $119 million.With four additions and one exclusion, the number of constituents in the MSCI Emerging Markets Standard Index will rise to 168 from 165. India's weight in the broader MSCI Emerging Markets Index is set to increase from 11.5% to 11.7%. The changes are broadly in line with Nuvama's expectations, except for ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, which avoided exclusion after its float factor was maintained.Read more: New SIP registrations fall 20%, stoppage ratio climbs to 116% in October after 5-month declineAlso 11 stocks will see their weights increase in the Standard Index. These include Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent of Groww; Lenskart Solutions; JSW Steel; Adani Energy Solutions; Coal India; One 97 Communications (Paytm); Bharat Forge; Oracle Financial Services Software; Zydus Lifesciences; Vedanta; and Bosch.Nuvama estimates that the increase in weights could bring passive inflows ranging from $10 million to $97 million into these stocks.Read more: Meesho block deal: SoftBank-backed entity likely to sell 1% stake worth Rs 1,174 croreNine stocks will see their weights decline: NTPC, Eicher Motors, Grasim Industries, REC, Hindustan Aeronautics, Cipla, GAIL India, MRF and Siemens India. The changes could result in outflows ranging from $10 million to $97 million, according to Nuvama.The MSCI Emerging Markets Small Cap Index will see 11 additions and 29 exclusions, taking the number of constituents down to 432 from 450. The stocks being added are PI Industries, Shadowfax Technologies, Apollo Micro Systems, HUDCO, Diamond Power Infrastructure, Aequs, Viyash Scientific, E2E Networks, SG Mart, Molbio Diagnostics and Axiscades Technologies.

Edelweiss Financial Services Q2 FY27 results: Profit rises 18% to ₹207 cr
items.summary:
Edelweiss Financial Services on Friday reported an 18 per cent growth in consolidated net profit to Rs 207 crore for the second quarter ended September.
The company had earned a profit of Rs 175 crore in the corresponding quarter of the preceding fiscal.
Total income increased to Rs 2,602 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared to Rs 1,900 crore in the year-ago period, Edelweiss Financial Services said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 720 crore from Rs 687 crore in the same quarter a year ago.
During the quarter, total expenses also rose to Rs 2,393 crore from Rs 1,946 crore in the same period a year ago.
The company completed the Rs 1,200-crore IPO of its subsidiary Edelweiss Alternatives last month.
Earlier this year, global investment management firm Carlyle became a strategic majority investor in another subsidiary of the company, Nido Home Finance, with an investment of Rs 2,000 crore.

HFCL bags export orders worth ₹834 crore for optical fibre cables
items.summary:
Telecom gear maker HFCL on Thursday said it has secured export orders worth about Rs 834.36 crore (around USD 88.94 million) for supplying optical fibre cables to an international customer, through its overseas wholly-owned subsidiary.
The order is scheduled for completion by June 2027.
The company, however, did not disclose the identity of the customer.
"These orders reaffirm the confidence reposed by our customers in the company's manufacturing capabilities, technological excellence and product quality," HFCL said in a regulatory filing.
HFCL posted a multi-fold jump in consolidated profit to Rs 394.22 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from Rs 72 crore a year ago, driven by demand for optical fibre cables from AI data centres.
The company has forecasted 80 per cent revenue growth in FY27 and expects to achieve the Rs 10,000 crore revenue mark before the projected timeline of FY29.

HFCL bags export orders worth ₹834 crore for optical fibre cables
items.summary:
Telecom gear maker HFCL on Thursday said it has secured export orders worth about Rs 834.36 crore (around USD 88.94 million) for supplying optical fibre cables to an international customer, through its overseas wholly-owned subsidiary.
The order is scheduled for completion by June 2027.
The company, however, did not disclose the identity of the customer.
"These orders reaffirm the confidence reposed by our customers in the company's manufacturing capabilities, technological excellence and product quality," HFCL said in a regulatory filing.
HFCL posted a multi-fold jump in consolidated profit to Rs 394.22 crore in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, up from Rs 72 crore a year ago, driven by demand for optical fibre cables from AI data centres.
The company has forecasted 80 per cent revenue growth in FY27 and expects to achieve the Rs 10,000 crore revenue mark before the projected timeline of FY29.

IIFL Finance shares rally 5% as Blackstone leads Rs 6,414 crore capital infusion
items.summary: IIFL Finance shares rallied as much as 4.90% to hit an intraday high of Rs 657.70 during Wednesday's trading session after the company announced a Rs 6,414 crore ($686 million) primary capital infusion led by global investment firm Blackstone and its promoters.The proposed fundraise is among the largest primary private equity investments in a listed Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC).In a regulatory filing, IIFL Finance said its board, at a meeting held on November 10, approved the capital raise through a preferential issue.Blackstone Private Equity will invest Rs 5,000 crore ($535 million) through a preferential allotment of compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS). These shares will convert into equity shares at Rs 602 apiece, in line with the regulatory pricing, within 18 months of allotment.Meanwhile, the company's promoters, Nirmal Jain and R. Venkataraman, will invest Rs 1,264 crore ($135 million) through a preferential allotment of warrants. Anchorage Capital will also participate in the transaction with a primary equity investment of Rs 150 crore ($16 million).The company and its promoters have entered into definitive agreements with Blackstone and Anchorage Capital for the proposed transaction, which remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals.According to  IIFL Finance,  the capital infusion will strengthen its capital adequacy, lower its cost of funds and accelerate growth in its gold finance business, a secured retail lending segment.The proceeds will also support IIFL Finance's ambition to emerge as one of India's largest diversified retail NBFCs.The company aims to tap Blackstone's global network and expertise in operations, technology, data and AI to expand its secured lending businesses, attract talent and strengthen its market position.The proposed appointment of Blackstone representatives to the company's board is also expected to enhance governance standards and oversight.Welcoming the investment, founder and Managing Director of IIFL Finance Nirmal Jain said the partnership would provide the company with additional capital to expand its businesses, invest in technology and deepen co-lending partnerships with banks while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk and capital.Also read: Kalyan Jewellers shares surge 10% to hit upper circuit on strong Q2 earningsIIFL Finance share price performance and Technical indicatorsIIFL Finance shares have gained around 11% over the past week. The stock currently commands a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 26,838 crore. Centre's EV push puts electric mobility stocks in the fast lane; M&M, Ola Electric lead rally with gains of up to 5%
items.summary: Shares of automobile and electric vehicle companies gained on Wednesday, November 11, following the Centre's decision to make electric vehicles the default choice for staff-car procurement by government ministries and departments, while doubling the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for electric cars to Rs 20 lakh. Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and Ola Electric Mobility emerged among the top gainers in the sector, with the former leading the rally with an intra-day gain of nearly 5%.M&M climbed 4.81% to touch an intra-day high of Rs 3,449, while Ola Electric Mobility advanced 3.53% to Rs 35.16.Hyundai Motor India was another major gainer, rising 3.08% to an intra-day high of Rs 2,175, while TVS Motor Company gained 2.89% to Rs 4,636.10. Ather Energy advanced 2.40% to Rs 1,904.50.Among other automobile companies, Maruti Suzuki India rose 2.10% to Rs 13,199, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 2.03% to Rs 301. JBM Auto advanced 2% to Rs 511.95, while Bajaj Auto registered the lowest gain among the nine stocks, rising 1.28% to Rs 11,120.At the last check, M&M was trading 4.5% higher, followed by TVS Motor Company, which was up 2.53%. Ola Electric Mobility gained 2.20%, while Hyundai Motor India advanced 2.3%. Maruti Suzuki India was up 2%, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ather Energy gained 1.5% each. Bajaj Auto and JBM Auto were trading 0.5% higher each, while Ashok Leyland was flat.ALSO READ: Earnings recovery, FII revival: 5 factors that will shape Dalal Street's next move after Q2What does the Centre's new EV procurement policy say?The Department of Expenditure (DEA), under the Ministry of Finance, has revised the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for the procurement of staff cars by government ministries and departments, doubling the limit for electric vehicles to Rs 20 lakh from Rs 10 lakh for internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.Under the revised instructions, electric vehicles have been made the default choice for government staff-car procurement. Ministries and departments are directed to ordinarily procure EVs when purchasing or replacing their existing staff cars.However, the revised instructions do not completely prohibit the purchase of conventional vehicles. Departments that consider EV procurement or deployment impractical can propose purchasing ICE vehicles, subject to justification and case-specific relaxation from the Department of Expenditure, with the required approvals.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser.
